capabilities.title: Use a manager to decompose work, bounded workers to execute specialist missions, and an inspector to review results
capabilities.sourceEvidence: README.md Role Templates and Usage Flow

capabilities.title: Keep the manager responsible for assignment, coordination, and the final operator-facing result
capabilities.sourceEvidence: README.md Quick Start and manager role description

capabilities.title: Represent specialist work as a structured mission with identity, assignment, completion status, and result summary
capabilities.sourceEvidence: README.md squad task create, ack, complete, requeue, and list commands

capabilities.title: Return machine-readable worker output with status, result, evidence, risks, verification, and next action
Route tasks according to worker role and declared capabilities
capabilities.sourceEvidence: README.md Agent Capability Metadata and protocol-derived support booleans

capabilities.title: Allow independent workers to return in one manager run while preventing unbounded fan-out
capabilities.sourceEvidence: README.md multiple worker terminals and automatic worker ID suffixes

capabilities.title: Preserve manager control when a worker fails or returns an invalid envelope
capabilities.sourceEvidence: README.md task requeue, leave preserving unread work, and doctor diagnostics

capabilities.title: Show the manager and worker phases before or during execution
capabilities.sourceEvidence: README.md Usage Flow and terminal role topology

capabilities.title: Persist messages, task state, results, and timestamps for later history inspection
capabilities.sourceEvidence: README.md How It Works, Message Flow, pending, and history commands
capabilities.reason: Nexus deliberately keeps specialist context inside the bounded operator-visible runtime trace. Persisting worker messages would duplicate potentially sensitive prompt and evidence content without a separate retention and deletion contract.

capabilities.title: Let workers acknowledge leases and let the manager requeue or reassign interrupted tasks
capabilities.sourceEvidence: README.md task ack, complete, requeue, and list commands
capabilities.reason: Nexus specialists are short-lived advisory calls, not durable background workers. Lease ownership, requeue, and reassignment would require a second resumable worker platform rather than improving the bounded in-app orchestrator.

capabilities.title: Track worker liveness, replaced sessions, protocol compatibility, and recovery diagnostics
capabilities.sourceEvidence: src/main.rs session token checks and doctor command
capabilities.reason: There are no persistent Nexus worker processes or sessions to heartbeat or replace. Request timeouts and typed failed handoffs are the complete lifecycle for the existing advisory-worker model.

capabilities.title: Support replies, direct notes, broadcast messages, and task-linked discussion between workers
capabilities.reason: Workers are intentionally isolated and can return only typed handoffs to MAX. Freeform cross-worker messaging would create an unreviewed prompt-propagation channel and bypass the central synthesis boundary.

capabilities.title: Load arbitrary Markdown roles and YAML team templates from each project
capabilities.sourceEvidence: README.md Role Templates and Team Templates
capabilities.reason: Nexus intentionally keeps one governed five-agent taxonomy. Arbitrary durable roles would recreate an unbounded second agent platform.

capabilities.title: Install Squad slash commands into Claude, Gemini, Codex, and OpenCode configuration folders
capabilities.reason: The Nexus orchestrator is an in-app runtime feature and does not modify external AI tool configuration.

capabilities.title: Launch tiled external AI terminals and optionally create isolated Git worktrees
capabilities.reason: Nexus reuses its existing local AI runtime and review gate; starting external terminals or Git worktrees would be a separate operator workflow.

capabilities.title: Install the Rust CLI and coordinate agents through a project-local SQLite database
capabilities.sourceEvidence: README.md How It Works and Cargo.toml dependencies
capabilities.reason: The capability is implemented natively through the existing TypeScript agent and API layers, so vendoring a parallel CLI and state store would duplicate the runtime.
